title: A Letters for the Vow
premise: August Sandoval built a career on other people's voices, ghostwriting a memoir for publishing titan Marguerite Hale while quietly nursing a decade-old wound: the love of her twenties, Elise Marchetti, who left to become Marguerite's star editor. When a blizzard traps August, Elise, and Marguerite at a remote Vermont inn for a deadline retreat, August's secret manuscript—the memoir Elise is editing, written in Marguerite's voice—becomes impossible to hide. As the snow seals the roads, old love and new ambition collide, and August must choose between the career that rescued her from obscurity and Elise, who finally reads between every line and sees her. In the end, August walks away from the ghostwriting contract, publishes her own book under her own name, and chooses Elise—learning that belonging was never something to be written for someone else.
about_author: Ivo Villalobos is a former speechwriter who spent eight years putting words in other people's mouths before turning to fiction. He writes from a farmhouse in upstate New York, where he insists the snowstorms are research.

chapters.title: The Voice That Isn't Hers
chapters.summary: August's POV. In a Brooklyn walk-up, August ghostwrites the opening chapters of Marguerite Hale's memoir, erasing herself sentence by sentence. A call from her agent confirms the deadline retreat in Vermont—where Elise Marchetti, the editor, will be present. Emotional beat: the ache of professional self-erasure and the dread of seeing Elise again.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Past Tense
chapters.summary: August's POV, flashback-woven. Packing for Vermont, August rereads an unsent letter from her twenties—the letter that never reached Elise before Elise left for New York. She buries it in a suitcase pocket. Emotional beat: grief disguised as practicality; love kept deliberately archived.

chapters.title: The Last Train North
chapters.summary: August's POV. On the train to Vermont, August rehearses a persona: invisible, professional, untouchable. She spots Elise in the same car, older, sharper, wearing a ring of quiet authority. They exchange two careful sentences. Emotional beat: the electric terror of proximity to someone who once knew everything.

chapters.title: The Inn at Hollow Brook
chapters.summary: Elise's POV. Elise arrives at the inn first, reviewing Marguerite's partial manuscript and noticing a voice in it that feels oddly, hauntingly familiar. Marguerite arrives late, imperious, announcing the retreat's terms: finish the memoir in five days. Emotional beat: Elise's unease—she recognizes craft, not yet the person behind it.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: August's POV. The storm arrives early and violently; the roads close, the power flickers, and the three are stranded with no cell signal. Marguerite declares the isolation 'a gift.' August watches Elise across candlelight. Emotional beat: claustrophobia turning into unwanted intimacy—there is nowhere left to hide.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Rules
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Over a tense dinner, Marguerite lays down the retreat's structure: daily readings of new chapters, no outside contact, total devotion to the book. She reveals, offhand, that her 'collaborator' will remain anonymous even from Elise. Emotional beat: Marguerite's control masking her own fear of being truly known.

chapters.title: The First Reading
chapters.summary: Elise's POV. Marguerite reads the new chapter aloud, but Elise recognizes the cadence—the parenthetical asides, the way grief is deflected with wit. It's the voice of the woman she loved at twenty-four. She says nothing. Emotional beat: recognition dawning like a slow sunrise, and the discipline of silence.

chapters.title: Snowbound Kitchen
chapters.summary: August's POV. Past midnight, August and Elise collide in the inn's kitchen, unable to sleep. They cook, argue about a sentence in the manuscript, and nearly touch. Elise asks what August has been writing 'for herself.' August lies. Emotional beat: the muscle memory of intimacy fighting ten years of armor.

chapters.title: What the Storm Takes
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The power fails entirely. Marguerite, forced into candlelight and stillness, begins dictating true memories to August—her real failures, the daughter she lost touch with. August writes it down, moved despite herself. Emotional beat: Marguerite's first crack of honesty; power revealed as loneliness.

chapters.title: The Unsent Letter
chapters.summary: August's POV. Elise, helping unpack August's bag, finds the decade-old letter and reads it before she can stop. The room goes silent. She doesn't confront August—yet—but she returns it with shaking hands and one sentence: 'You never sent this.' Emotional beat: the past tense shattering; exposure without resolution.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Library
chapters.summary: Elise's POV. Elise corners August: 'It's you. The memoir. It was always you.' August admits everything—the ghostwriting, the silence, the choice to stay invisible. Elise's fury isn't about the secret; it's that August let her believe she'd been forgotten. Emotional beat: betrayal and longing fused; the truth costs them both.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Bargain
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite, sensing the fracture, offers August a career-making deal: her name on the memoir's acknowledgment page, a two-book deal, a seat at the table—contingent on absolute discretion and finishing the manuscript. Emotional beat: the corruption of power offering a golden cage precisely when love is on the line.

chapters.title: The Chapter That Wasn't Hers
chapters.summary: August's POV. August writes the memoir's most vulnerable chapter—Marguerite's story, but saturated with her own heartbreak—and reads it aloud at the morning session. Elise listens with tears she refuses to explain. Marguerite, for once, is silent. Emotional beat: art as confession; the mask becoming the face.

chapters.title: Thaw Line
chapters.summary: Elise's POV. A brief break in the storm lets Elise hike to the ridge for signal. Her firm is demanding the manuscript early; her boss wants Marguerite's 'collaborator' named and contracted exclusively. Elise realizes protecting August may cost her own standing. Emotional beat: duty pulling against love, the same choice August faces, mirrored.

chapters.title: One Night, No Drafts
chapters.summary: August's POV. The storm returns; the inn loses the generator. By candlelight, August and Elise stop performing. They speak plainly—about the letter, the leaving, the years—and cross a line neither can uncross. Emotional beat: surrender; love admitted in present tense for the first time.

chapters.title: The Morning After the Storm
chapters.summary: Elise's POV. Morning brings plows, signal, and consequences. Marguerite discovers the relationship and invokes the bargain: finish the book, keep the deal, walk away from Elise—or lose everything August has built. Emotional beat: the golden cage snapping shut; duty dressed as opportunity.

chapters.title: Invisible Ink
chapters.summary: August's POV. August drafts the memoir's final chapter and realizes every ending she writes for Marguerite is an ending she's refusing to write for herself. She visits Marguerite's room at night and finds her alone, unguarded, reading her daughter's letters. Emotional beat: August sees the cost of Marguerite's choices—her own possible future.

chapters.title: The Choice on the Ridge
chapters.summary: August's POV. August tells Marguerite she's done: no acknowledgment page, no two-book deal, no more borrowed voice. Marguerite, in a final act of power, threatens to erase August's contribution entirely. August signs nothing. Emotional beat: the climax of the internal war—selfhood chosen over security.

chapters.title: What Marguerite Kept
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Alone with the finished manuscript, Marguerite reads the dedication August left in the draft—'for the one who reads between the lines'—and understands everything. She makes her own choice, calling her estranged daughter before she calls her publisher. Emotional beat: the antagonist's quiet redemption; power relinquished, not defeated.

chapters.title: Byline
chapters.summary: Elise's POV. The roads open. Elise resigns her firm rather than enforce Marguerite's exclusivity clause, betting her career on August's name. At the inn's door, she finds August waiting with the unsent letter, finally postmarked, and a new manuscript titled with her own name. Emotional beat: mutual choice; both women stepping out of hiding.

chapters.title: The Book That Was Hers
chapters.summary: August's POV, six months later. August's own memoir publishes—small, honest, hers. At the launch, Marguerite appears, acknowledges August's hand in her book publicly, and introduces her daughter to the room. Elise reads the dedication aloud, laughing. Emotional beat: vindication without vengeance; the voice reclaimed.

chapters.title: A Letter for the Vow
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, epilogue. One year later, in the same Vermont inn, August and Elise exchange vows they write themselves—and read each other's first. The unsent letter is framed above the fireplace. Marguerite sends a single line: 'Some books are only the first draft.' Emotional beat: belonging, at last, in present tense.
